title: How a former DeepMind researcher raised at a $300M pre-seed valuation before launching a product
slides: What did a DeepMind alum sell for $300M without a product?
It was a pre-seed round, valuing the idea alone.
The company has zero revenue and no public beta.
Your pitch deck now competes with invisible rocketships.
Re-evaluate your valuation after this week's fundraising.
thread_text:
1. No product. $300M.

DeepMind alum raised a pre-seed round valuing the idea alone. Zero revenue, no beta.

2. The invisible rocketship.

Investors priced a company with zero traction. Your deck now competes with pure narrative.

3. A new asset class.

Pre-seed is betting on reputation and story, not data. You can't A/B test that.

4. Valuation whiplash.

One non-existent company resets the ceiling. Your $5M ask just shifted to $10M—or $0.

5. Re-run your numbers.

Take your current deck and delete all product screenshots. Is the valuation still defensible? Do it this week.
